channel.title: Market Pressure Map · Indian markets
channel.description: Daily news scored for its impact on Indian market sectors and the rupee, bonds, inflation and foreign flows.

item.title: GST collections jump 22.9% to ₹2.31 lakh crore in October, fastest growth in over four years
item.description:
Domestic GST rose 15.8% to ₹1.59 lakh crore and import GST was ₹72,246 crore; net collections rose about 26% to ₹2.03 lakh crore. Fourth straight month above ₹2 lakh crore. Strengthening.

Why it matters: Strong festive consumption and higher import values lift tax revenue, offsetting part of the subsidy-driven widening of the fiscal deficit.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance +2, Growth outlook +1

Confidence: high · horizon: months

item.title: Manufacturing PMI eases to 54.7 in October from 55.1, below the 54.9 flash; export orders at six-month high
item.description:
Output and new orders growth slowed, finished-goods stocks rose at a record pace and selling-price inflation neared a four-year low. Composite flash was a four-month high. Steady, slightly slower.

Why it matters: Still-solid expansion and easing price pressure support earnings and the inflation outlook, while record inventories hint at softer production ahead.

Market gauges: Growth outlook −1, Inflation outlook +1

Confidence: high · horizon: weeks

item.title: Passenger vehicle dispatches cross a record 5 lakh in October, up about 12–15% from 4.6 lakh
item.description:
Festive demand, tax changes and lower borrowing costs drove dispatches; the market leader grew 20%. Retail registrations may shift into November. New record.

Why it matters: Record vehicle demand supports automakers, component makers and auto lenders and signals resilient urban consumption despite high fuel prices.

Market gauges: Growth outlook +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: Brent falls up to 3% to about $110–112 in Asia as Iran–Qatar talks continue; OPEC+ holds December output
item.description:
No new escalation over the weekend after Friday's $117.64 six-month high. OPEC+ kept targets unchanged. Easing after an October surge.

Why it matters: A pullback trims India's import bill and inflation risk, but prices above $110 and post-election strike risk keep pressure high.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance +1, Inflation outlook +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: days

item.title: US says no decision on Iran strikes before the 3 November vote; Israel reportedly urges strikes right after
item.description:
The US president says there is no hurry or timetable for a deal; talks continue via Qatari mediators and Iran's two-day reopening plan. Strike risk rises after Tuesday.

Why it matters: The days after the US vote are a key oil risk window for India: strikes would lift crude, hurt the rupee and equities; a deal would bring relief.

Market gauges: Equities (Nifty & Sensex) −1, Fiscal & trade balance −1

Confidence: low · horizon: days

item.title: Rupee slips 21 paise to 94.97 per dollar in early trade as the dollar strengthens
item.description:
It opened at 94.90; falling crude limited losses. An analyst sees a 94.40–95.60 range after October's best month since February. Pause after gains.

Why it matters: A firm dollar offsets oil relief; a stable rupee near 95 keeps imported inflation contained.

Market gauges: Rupee −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: days

item.title: Qatari LNG tanker with six Indians aboard attacked near Hormuz; crew safe
item.description:
The Pakistan-bound carrier was hit despite reported Iranian approval; Iran also claims two more tankers hit mines. First attack on LNG shipping in this round. Escalating.

Why it matters: Attacks on LNG carriers threaten India's recovering Qatari gas supply, raising costs for power, fertiliser and city gas.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: India's oil imports hit a record 5.6 million barrels a day
item.description:
Strong refinery runs and flexible buying between Gulf and Russian grades. Follows record October LNG imports. Ongoing.

Why it matters: Record volumes at high prices swell the import bill and dollar demand, though strong runs support fuel exports.

Market gauges: Fiscal & trade balance −1, Rupee −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks
